# cws-mcp

> MCP server for Chrome Web Store extension management. Upload, publish, and manage Chrome extensions from any MCP-compatible AI agent.

## Tools (12)

- upload: Upload a ZIP file to Chrome Web Store (updates existing item draft)
- publish: Publish an extension with optional staged rollout, publish type, and skip-review
- status: Fetch current status including review state, deploy percentage, and version
- cancel: Cancel a pending submission
- deploy-percentage: Set staged rollout percentage (0-100, must exceed current target)
- get: Legacy metadata read; blocked after 2026-10-15 00:00 UTC. Use status for review/version/rollout; read listing metadata in the Developer Dashboard.
- update-metadata: Legacy metadata write; blocked after 2026-10-15 00:00 UTC. Edit listing metadata in the Developer Dashboard.
- submit: One-shot upload → publish → status in a single call (with existence-check preflight and readable errors)
- rollback: Re-publish a previously published version under a new higher version number; no review, discards pending/staged submissions, aborts percentage rollouts. Validate first with validateOnly=true.
- reviews: Fetch user reviews (pagination, orderBy rating / create_time desc, filter "rating = N")
- rating-summary: Average rating, rating count, per-star counts
- metrics: Query installs, installs-7d, uninstalls, users, users-7d, impressions, page-views over YYYY-MM-DD dates, optionally sliced by one dimension
- upload/submit require confirmed upload completion (SUCCEEDED or compatible SUCCESS without itemError). Pending or unknown completion returns an error and submit does not publish; no automatic polling. Check status before publishing alone. lastAsyncUploadState covers only the latest asynchronous upload within 24 hours; verify the intended draft in the Developer Dashboard if ambiguous or another upload occurred.
- status summaries include takenDown/warned flags and lastAsyncUploadState when provided; active policy flags require Developer Dashboard review.

## Install

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cws-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@kagayoi/cws-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "CWS_CLIENT_ID": "xxxxx.apps.googleusercontent.com",
        "CWS_CLIENT_SECRET": "GOCSPX-xxxxx",
        "CWS_REFRESH_TOKEN": "1//xxxxx",
        "CWS_PUBLISHER_ID": "me",
        "CWS_ITEM_ID": "your-extension-id"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Environment Variables

Authentication: provide EITHER a service account (Auth A, recommended for CI/CD) OR the OAuth2 trio (Auth B). The server prefers the service account when both are present.

- CWS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY (Auth A): Service account JSON key — a file path or the raw JSON
- CWS_CLIENT_ID (Auth B): Google OAuth2 Client ID
- CWS_CLIENT_SECRET (Auth B): Google OAuth2 Client Secret
- CWS_REFRESH_TOKEN (Auth B): OAuth2 Refresh Token
- CWS_PUBLISHER_ID (optional): Publisher ID, defaults to "me"
- CWS_ITEM_ID (optional): Default extension item ID

## API Coverage

Supports these Chrome Web Store API v2 endpoints: media.upload, publishers.items.publish, publishers.items.fetchStatus, publishers.items.cancelSubmission, publishers.items.setPublishedDeployPercentage, publishers.items.rollback, publishers.items.fetchReviews, publishers.items.getRatingSummary, publishers.items.queryMetrics. Legacy v1.1 metadata tools remain registered but are blocked after the cutoff. Resource reads also skip v1 after the cutoff and return metadata.unavailable alongside v2 status. This server is API only and does not automate the browser.

## Notes

- deploy-percentage only works for extensions with 10,000+ seven-day active users
- Rollout percentage must always increase (never decrease)
- Do not call get or update-metadata after the v1.1 cutoff (2026-10-15 00:00 UTC); read/change listing metadata manually in the Chrome Web Store Developer Dashboard. The v2 API has no metadata read/write endpoint.
- The Chrome Web Store API cannot create items; create new items manually in the Developer Dashboard
